headline: No entry is distinguishable from luck once the family of trials and the week-clustered uncertainty are both counted. The best record is real; its interpretation as skill is not supported.

chance_null.question: Could a coin flip have produced this record?
chance_null.reading: 37 of 57 against a 50/50 benchmark. Single-test tail 0.0166.

family_null.question: Could the best of the whole family have produced it?
family_null.reading: 21 variants were tried. The best of 21 coin-flip runs reaches 37 or more 0.296 of the time at n=57.

permutation_null.question: Did the probabilities carry information beyond each week's balance?

required_n.question: How long before a real edge is even visible?

required_n.reading: A 57-game evaluation window cannot separate a 55% model from a 50% one: at 80% power a 55% model betting the breakeven rate needs 2,241 settled selections, which is 173 weeks at this season's 13 games a week, or 8.2 full 272-game seasons. At 57.5% the requirement falls to 585.

luck_band.question: What does luck look like at this n, judged as one test?
luck_band.reading: This band is a single-test statement: 37 wins sits just above an upper bound of 35. The family null above is the one that governs, and it does not clear.

why_not_removed: One season of scored games, so no season-level holdout exists (PG-SEASONS).
No executable price, so a probability better than chance cannot become a return (PG-PRICE-SOURCE).
No pre-kickoff forecast has been recorded, so nothing here is prospective (PG-PROSPECTIVE).
The development and evaluation windows order the entries differently, which is what noise looks like.

rejected_alternative.why: Return is one draw from a distribution whose spread at n=57 dwarfs any plausible edge. The power table above is the arithmetic: a 55% model needs 2,846 settled selections to be seen at 80% power. Ranking on return would order the table by the noise term. Ranking on a cluster lower bound of a proper score at least orders it by evidence, and still refuses to qualify anything.
